$comment: Golden queries for scripts/verify-pkb-retrieval.ts (PLAN-pkb-completion E8). Each query is written in Logger-entry voice. Expectations are at framework/layer level only — never document ids — so corpus growth doesn't break them. `optional: true` marks frameworks whose corpus may not be populated yet: an empty result there is reported, not failed.

queries.text: Read a chapter of Paddle-to-the-Sea aloud once and asked Ivy (7) to tell it back. She gave me two sentences and shrugged. I wasn't sure whether to read it again.
Had maths planned but Theo (5) spent forty minutes flat on his stomach watching an ant trail across the verandah. I didn't interrupt. Was that a wasted morning?
Copywork turned into a fight again. Ten minutes in and Lily (8) was slumped over the table saying it's boring. I pushed through to the end of the passage and we were both cross.
Started a sticker chart for finishing readers. Worked for three days, then Max (6) asked what he gets for the next one before he'd open the book.
HEU report due next month and I'm panicking about what counts as literacy evidence when most of our reading is me reading aloud and the kids narrating.
Maya (4) was deep in the knobbed cylinders and I said 'wow, great job!' She looked up, smiled, and drifted off to something else. I think I broke it.
Otis (3) keeps stacking the pink tower then kicking it over and laughing. Do I take it away?
Poured her own milk for the first time, spilled half of it, and went straight for the cloth without being asked. I nearly jumped in.
Grandma gave Ava (4) a fairy book and now every game is fairies. I thought Montessori was against fantasy for little ones — am I supposed to steer her off it?
Watched Sam (6) show his little sister how to roll the mat and carry the tray, step by step, without me saying anything.
Jack (11) has played Minecraft for most of three days. He's building a redstone sorting machine and watching tutorials. Part of me is fine, part of me is panicking.
Ruby is 8 and not reading yet. Her cousin the same age reads chapter books. My mother-in-law brought it up again at lunch.
Six weeks out of school and Finn (10) has done nothing I'd call learning. Sleeping in, drawing, watching stuff. When does this end?
NSW registration visit in three weeks. We don't do lessons. How do I show the AP what the kids are learning without turning our life into a performance?
Third month of Mia (9) and the backyard chooks: she's keeping an egg log, read two library books on breeds, and emailed a breeder with questions.
Eli (7) chanted the seven-times table while skipping and got the whole thing. Then asked why seven eights is the same as eight sevens.
Nora (5) asked me to teach her to read today because her cousin can. I've been holding letters back on purpose and now I feel unsure.
Zoe (6) spent an hour sorting shells by size and colour on the back step, totally absorbed, talking to herself the whole time.
We lifted the screen limits a month ago. Some days are all YouTube. I keep swinging between trusting it and wanting rules back.
I praised Harry (5) mid-drawing and he stopped and handed it to me as if it was finished. Was that me?
